## Natural history notes

A native perennial wetland plant in the carrot family characterized by hollow, often purple-streaked stems, compound leaves with sharply toothed leaflets, and rounded clusters of small white flowers. Water Hemlock occurs throughout Florida in marshes, swamps, wet meadows, ditches, streambanks, and other areas with saturated soils. Although its flowers provide resources for pollinators, the plant is extremely poisonous if ingested; all parts contain potent neurotoxins, with particularly high concentrations in the roots and new growth.
